para: Beyond its role within the theory of logical calculi, the subclassical graph has a structural relationship to quantum computing that warrants remark even at this preliminary stage. The logical operations of a quantum gate act on qubits in a non-classical setting: the conjunction and disjunction of quantum states do not satisfy the classical structural rules of Weakening and Contraction, and the measurement process introduces an asymmetry between the left and right sides of the information-flow relation that has a precise proof-theoretic analogue in the restriction from LK to LJ. The duality operations of , applied to the fragment of the subclassical graph that includes linear logic and its extensions, generate a family of calculi whose sequent structure corresponds to the algebraic structure of the quantum circuit model. Whether this correspondence is merely a structural analogy or a substantive theoretical connection — whether the subclassical graph can be made to serve as the logical foundation for a theory of quantum computation in the same way that classical propositional logic underlies the Boolean circuit model — is an open question. It is the right question. Its investigation begins with the construction that this chapter has described.
